title: Few pairs far apart in a diameter-one planar set
statement: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ be points in the Euclidean plane $\bbr^2$ whose set $\{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$ has diameter exactly $1$. Then the number of unordered pairs $\{x_i, x_j\}$ whose Euclidean distance satisfies $d(x_i, x_j) > 1/\sqrt{2}$ is at most $\lfloor n^2/3 \rfloor$.
hypotheses_covered: n points in the Euclidean plane
the set of points has diameter equal to 1
